review: 1:1–1:2 בְּצִלְּךָ … אֶחְפְּצָה לָשָׁבֶת — Song of Songs 2:3 (בְּצִלּוֹ חִמַּדְתִּי וְיָשַׁבְתִּי); the Arabic تَحْتَ ظِلِّكَ … أَشْتَهِي أَنْ أَجْلِسَ is that verse, and the Hebrew keeps חָמַד ('to desire') even though the Arabic uses a different verb.

2:1–2:4 אֶמְצָא אֶת־הַסֵּפֶר … פְּרִי מָתוֹק לְחִכִּי — the Arabic أَجِدُ الْكِتَابَ لِي / ثَمَرًا يَحْلُو لِحَلْقِي is 'I find the Book for me, fruit sweet to my palate'; the Hebrew keeps the book as a found object and the taste as its effect, with חֵךְ as the biblical palate (Ps 119:103).

2:5–2:6 חִכְּךָ … כֻּלּוֹ מַחֲמַדִּים — Song 5:16 (חִכּוֹ מַמְתַקִּים וְכֻלּוֹ מַחֲמַדִּים); the Arabic حَلْقُكَ … كُلُّهُ مُشْتَهَيَات is that verse, and the Hebrew keeps the Song's rare noun מַחֲמַדִּים which the Arabic paraphrases.

1:7–1:8 אֵיךְ בְּדָמוֹ זָכַנִי / חֶסֶד לְעוֹלָם — the Arabic كَيْفَ بِالدَّمِ حَبَانِي / رَحْمَةً طُولَ الْمَدَى is 'how with His blood He endowed me with mercy evermore'; זָכָה is used in its biblical sense of being granted a share (Num 5:28), so the line is a gift received, not a merit earned.
The refrain בְּצִלְּךָ, אֲהוּבִי opens stanzas 1 and 2 at the same two positions the Arabic repeats تَحْتَ ظِلِّكَ حَبِيبِي, and the 8-line stanza shape is kept from the print (2 stanzas of 8).
